title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Introduction states: "applying key layer gating (G3) yields superior performance improvements compared to SDPA or value gating, reducing PPL by up to 0.3 and improving MMLU significantly." This directly contradicts the paper's own results. Table 1 row 7 (k Elementwise G_3) shows PPL = 6.016 vs baseline 6.026 (improvement of only 0.010, not 0.3), MMLU 59.18, and GSM8k 50.49 which is WORSE than baseline 52.92. Section 3.2.1 explicitly states the opposite: "SDPA and value output gating are effective. Inserting gates at the output of SDPA (G1) or the value map (G2) is the most effective." The PPL reduction of ~0.3 the intro attributes to G3 actually belongs to SDPA gating (G1: 6.026 -> 5.761 = 0.265). The introduction misstates the paper's central finding.

The Abstract claims "a comprehensive comparison over 40 variants of 30B MoE models and 3.4B dense models trained on a 1 trillion token dataset." The body reports entirely different experimental scale: Section 3.1 states "We conduct experiments on both MoE models (15B total parameters with 2.54B activated, 15A2B) and dense models (1.7B total parameters)." Table 1 tests 15 gating variants (not 40) on 400B tokens; Table 2 reports 400B/1T/3.5T token runs. The abstract's model sizes (30B MoE, 3.4B dense) are exactly 2x the body's (15B MoE, 1.7B dense), and the token budget / variant count do not match any setting in the body. This is a stale, internally-inconsistent abstract.

The text claims: "When increasing the maximum LR, both baselines and gating variants frequently encounter convergence issues (row 6, 12), with some gating models diverging silently." Table 2 rows 6 and 12, cited in the parenthetical, are BOTH labeled "Baseline" (LR 8.0 x 10^-3) and are the rows that diverge (all cells '-'). The gating variants at the same LR (row 10 'SDPA Elementwise' LR 8e-3: PPL 7.325; row 14 'SDPA Elementwise' LR 8e-3: PPL 7.078) converged. No gating model row in Table 2 diverges. The claim that gating models diverged is contradicted by the paper's own table, and the cited rows reference baselines, not gating variants.

Table 4 row 5 ("Value Elementwise Gate") reports GSM8k = 51.33, while Table 1 row 6 ("v Elementwise G_2") reports GSM8k = 53.97 for the identical model configuration (value-position elementwise sigmoid gating on the 15A2B MoE). The other shared metrics match exactly between the two tables (PPL 5.820, HellaSwag 74.38, MMLU 59.17), confirming the two rows describe the same model. A 2.64-point discrepancy in GSM8k for the same configuration is an internal data contradiction.

Section 5.1 cites reference numbers [80], [81], and [82]: "Several works on state-space models [3, 10, 57, 80] and Linear Attention variants, including the recently proposed DeltaGate model [81]... The novel gating formulation in AlphaFold2 [5], Forgetting Transformer [6], and the unseen GatorNet [82] architecture provide critical foundations." The reference list ends at [71] (OpenAI GPT-OSS model card). There are no bibliography entries for [80], [81], or [82], making these dangling references with no corresponding bibliographic record in the paper.

Section 4.2 reads: "We analyze the gating scores (Tab. 1, 'Gate Score' column) of models with gating applied at the value (G2) and SDPA output (G1) positions." Table 1 has no 'Gate Score' column; its columns are Method, Act Func, Score Shape, Added Param, Avg PPL, HellaSwag, MMLU, GSM8k, C-Eval. The 'Gate Score' column (along with M-Act and F-Attn) actually appears in Table 4. The in-text table reference is incorrect and misdirects the reader.

summary: Exhaustive verification (lenient strictness) of 'Gated Attention for Large Language Models' found 6 internal inconsistencies, none in the mathematics. All 9 equations (Eqs. 1-9) are algebraically correct, including the low-rank W_V/W_O merging argument in Eq. 6. The reported RULER deltas (Table 5) are internally consistent within rounding, and the parameter accounting for elementwise/headwise gates (Table 1 rows 5-11) checks out. The problems are concentrated in cross-section consistency: (1) the Abstract describes 30B MoE / 3.4B dense models trained on 1T tokens, while the body reports 15A2B MoE (15B) / 1.7B dense models on 400B-3.5T tokens; (2) the Introduction claims key-layer gating (G3) is the best variant and reduces PPL by ~0.3, directly contradicting Table 1 and Sec. 3.2.1 where SDPA (G1) and value (G2) gating are best and G3 is near-baseline (PPL 6.016 vs 6.026); (3) Sec. 3.2.2 claims gating models diverged at high LR, but the diverging Table 2 rows (6, 12) are baselines while the gated rows (10, 14) converged; (4) Table 4 row 5 and Table 1 row 6 report different GSM8k (51.33 vs 53.97) for the identical value-gated configuration; (5) references [80], [81], [82] are cited in Sec. 5.1 but absent from a reference list that ends at [71]; (6) Sec. 4.2 points to a 'Gate Score' column in Table 1 that exists only in Table 4. Because findings 1-3 exceed the 0.85 confidence threshold, the paper requires correction; the three high-confidence issues concern the paper's stated experimental scale and its own central result, making the report not ready as written.
